title: memory / {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %}
content: ## {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %} Sessions that use the {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness locally can use {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %}, the same cloud memory service used by {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %}, {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cloud_agent %}, and code review. Memories captured by one supported feature can inform another, although supported scopes vary. For example, code review uses repository facts, not user preferences. ### Set up cloud-backed memory {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %} is on by default in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}. To use it: 1. [Sign in to {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot %}](/docs/setup/copilot.md) with your {% data variables.product.prodname_github %} account. 1. In your [personal {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} settings on {% data variables.product.prodname_github %}](https://github.com/settings/copilot/features), check that **{% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %}** is **Enabled**. If your plan is managed by an organization or enterprise, its policies must permit memory. 1. Check that `setting(chat.copilot.memory.enabled)` is on in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Settings. If you previously turned it off, it stays off until you turn it on. 1. Create or resume a local {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} session in the {% data variables.copilot.chat_view %} or {% data variables.copilot.agents_window %}. The setting applies to sessions created or resumed after it changes. The {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} editor preview-features policy doesn't control cloud memory. Repository memories require a {% data variables.product.prodname_github %}-hosted repository. User preferences are tied to your signed-in {% data variables.product.prodname_github %} account and can apply across repositories. If the setting is on but memory isn't available, check your {% data variables.product.prodname_github %} account settings and organization policies. Contact your administrator if a required feature is unavailable or locked. For account eligibility and default billing-entity requirements when you have multiple licenses, see [Managing {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %} for your personal account](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/copilot-memory/manage-for-yourself). ### Choose what to remember Cloud-backed memory has two scopes: | Scope | What it stores | Where it applies | |---|---|---| | **Repository** | Durable codebase facts and conventions, supported by citations to the code. | Shared with people who have access to the repository and {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %}. Used only for that repository. | | **User** | Coding and workflow preferences that apply across repositories. | Used in your own supported {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} interactions, not other contributors' interactions. | Storing repository facts requires write access to the repository and memory enabled for your account. On organization- or enterprise-managed plans, administrators can also review and delete user preferences. See [Managing {% data variables.copilot.copilot_memory %} for an organization or enterprise](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/copilot-memory/manage-as-administrator). > [!CAUTION] > Don't store credentials, secrets, or sensitive personal information in memory. Repository facts are shared, not private notes. Keep reviewed team requirements in source-controlled project documentation or [custom instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md). ### Store, recall, and correct memories Ask the agent to remember a durable convention or preference. State the scope when it matters: ```prompt Find how this repository verifies changes, and remember the command for this repository. ``` ```prompt Across all my repositories, remember that I prefer concise commit message subjects. ``` The agent recalls relevant repository facts and user preferences when a session starts. It uses **Store Memory** to save new information. When it verifies an existing memory, it can upvote it instead of storing a duplicate. It can downvote an outdated memory and store a corrected replacement. If a remembered convention is wrong, point the agent to the current code and ask it to correct the memory. Use persistent memory for durable information, not temporary task status. ### Review and delete cloud memories Review stored information on {% data variables.product.prodname_github %}: * **User preferences**: Open your [personal memory settings](https://github.com/settings/copilot/memory) to view and delete preferences. * **Repository facts**: With repository administration access, open the repository's **Settings** > **Copilot** > **Memory**. Deleting a repository fact removes it for everyone who uses memory in that repository. Asking the agent to forget a cloud memory downvotes it rather than permanently deleting it. To permanently delete it, use the {% data variables.product.prodname_github %} settings above. The local memory-file commands below don't delete cloud memories. Facts and preferences that go unused are automatically deleted after 28 days. Successful validation and use can reset that timer. Learn more about [memory retention and validation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/prompting-and-context/copilot-memory#retention-and-validation). To stop using cloud memory in newly created or resumed {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} sessions, turn off `setting(chat.copilot.memory.enabled)`. Your personal memory setting on {% data variables.product.prodname_github %} controls its use across supported {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} features. To remove stored information, delete it on {% data variables.product.prodname_github %}.
